rv.q: This is the first time this season that I'm itching to go back and re-experience it all over again.

Umberto Giordano's tragedy requires three singers with the vocal chops and dramatic instincts to deliver its soaring vocal lines and seething passions. The Met has assembled such a cast, and with Daniele Rustioni in the pit, the audience was swept up in a riveting performance of Giordano’s most enduring creation.
It showed that a fine and enjoyable Andrea Chénier experience is still possible in this new century; no need to live in the past.
